scope: Proposition 10.2 (Exterior sewing) of the manuscript “Uniform marked-polygon estimates and sharp finite bridge moments” (preprints/Uniform-marked-polygon-estimates-and-sharp-finite-bridge-moments-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e9b7a0252f329287), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 101. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the nested family, endpoint bin and deterministic chord event just specified, the following estimates hold. The average E includes the level and the support randomness, and the constants are uniform in the event and the admissible levels. 1. If it requires the use of two fixed internal links, the average satisfies E ≤ Cl3/4 K, where K is the single-polygon mass using those links on a cylinder of period vector of any lattice direction chosen for the marks and length sufficiently large compared with R. 2. For l large, suppose the goal instead is to extend to bridges between horizontal caps at heights near ±AR, A a sufficiently large constant (each height magnitude between AR and 2AR). Let B∗ count bridges between those caps, with base start free in a horizontal interval of size CR, containing the required chord event for at least one choice of the supports. One can replace the condition by any common weaker deterministic event (e.g. a length lower bound). Then B∗ ≥ cR−1/2 (l/R)C0 l1/2 E.
